title: Sell Mineral Rights in Stafford, OH
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Stafford, OH | Monroe County
metaDescription: Stafford, Monroe County mineral owner? Understand how well decline behavior in the Utica core affects what your interest is worth today versus later.
heroLead: A well near Stafford does not produce at the same rate forever, and understanding that decline curve is the difference between a rough guess and a real number when you are deciding whether to sell.
intro: Stafford is a small community in Monroe County, deep in the Utica/Point Pleasant core, an area that has drawn extensive horizontal development over the past decade. If your family holds a mineral or royalty interest tied to a well near Stafford, understanding how that well's production behaves over time is central to any honest conversation about selling.
Rather than guess, we look at the actual decline pattern for wells in your unit before putting a number in front of you.

sections.heading: How Utica wells typically decline
paragraphs: Horizontal Utica wells generally produce their highest volumes in the first several months, then decline steeply through the first couple of years before settling into a longer, shallower tail that can continue for a decade or more at reduced but still meaningful rates.

Where a specific well near Stafford sits on that curve, early high-rate production, mid-decline, or long-tail, changes how much future income the interest is likely to generate, and therefore what a fair offer looks like today.

sections.heading: Reading decline into your royalty history
paragraphs: If you have several months or years of royalty statements, plotting the volumes shows exactly where your interest sits on that curve. A steep recent drop suggests the well is still working through early decline, while a flatter recent trend suggests it has entered its long tail.
We use this pattern, along with current Ohio Department of Natural Resources production records, to build a hedged, activity-based offer rather than pricing off a single month's check.

sections.heading: Selling before versus after further decline
paragraphs: Some owners near Stafford prefer to sell early, while a well is still in a stronger production phase, to capture value now rather than watch it decline further. Others prefer to hold and collect ongoing royalty income for as long as the well continues to pay.
Both are reasonable choices, and understanding your well's specific decline stage is what lets you make that decision with real information instead of a guess.

faqs.question: How do I know where my well near Stafford is in its decline?
faqs.answer: Comparing several months or years of royalty statements shows the trend. We can also check state production records for the specific well if you know its name or API number.

faqs.question: Is it better to sell early or wait until the well is older?
faqs.answer: There is no single right answer. It depends on your own financial situation and how much certainty you want now versus the possibility of continued royalty income later.

faqs.question: Does Monroe County still see new drilling, or is it mostly older wells now?
faqs.answer: Monroe County has seen both established production and continued permitting activity in recent years. We check current records for the specific area near Stafford before quoting.
